question.problem: For a fixed temperature, the pressure $P$ of a gas varies inversely with the volume $V$ that it occupies. When $V=3\,{\text{m}}^{3},$ the pressure is $P=2$ megapascal ($\text{MPa}$). What will be the pressure if the gas is compressed to a container with volume $V=2\,{\text{m}}^{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
The pressure $P$ is inversely proportional to the volume $V,$ so we have

$$
P=\frac{k}{V},
$$

where $k$ is the constant of variation.

We are told that when the volume is $V=3\,{\text{m}}^{3},$ the pressure is $P=2$ megapascal ($\text{MPa}$). We can use this information to solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{k}{3} \\ 2\cdot 3 & =k \\ 6 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

We now have the equation

$$
P=\frac{6}{V}.
$$

We can use this equation to find the pressure when the volume is $V=2\,{\text{m}}^{3},$ as follows:

$$
P=\frac{6}{2}=3
$$

Therefore, the pressure of the gas when $V=2\,{\text{m}}^{3}$ is $3\,\text{MPa}.$
